protocol: per shape: warmup both arms, then reps x (fp8blk timed, q8_0 timed) INTERLEAVED inside the rep loop so both arms share one clock/thermal regime; median of reps; flock /tmp/gpu5090.lock. Weight operand is the SAME logical weight for both arms: the e4m3 codes are the source, and the Q8_0 slab is produced from them by the merged ARM B' device dequant, i.e. the actual floor path this kernel competes with. Denominator is RE-MEASURED in this session's regime — v1's recorded floor is never used as a cross-day denominator.
shapes: the 27B's own projection shapes (same list as the v1 lane's bench, so the ratios are directly comparable slice to slice)

change: scale block (128) becomes the OUTER k loop; the four k32 MMAs of a block chain into ONE unscaled f32 accumulator; (s_blk*dB) folds once per block. MMQ_ITER_K 256->128, x tile row 64->32 value-ints, smem 61KB->37KB. Activation scale granularity 32->128 (v2's own quantizer) is the arithmetic change that licenses the hoist.
kernel_check: ALL GREEN — 9 shapes, EXACT arm 0 bit mismatches + 0 NaN each, RAND arm rms_rel <= 1.47e-6, e4m3 code coverage 254/254
delta_vs_v1: +4.1pp q_proj, +4.2pp kv, +3.1pp o, +3.0pp gate_up, +2.0pp down, +3.1pp square — every shape improved, none reaches 1.0x
+5.5pp q_proj, +4.9pp kv, +3.9pp o, +4.1pp gate_up, +1.9pp down, +5.6pp square — square-ref reaches 0.992x, i.e. parity within the run's spread, but no shape exceeds the floor

change: occupancy: (a) halve MMQ_Y and nwarps TOGETHER (Y=64, 4 warps) with __launch_bounds__ minBlocks=2 — the w4a8 treatment, which does not duplicate weight reads; (b) keep Y=128 and ask the compiler for 2 CTA/SM (OCC=2) on the now-37KB tile.
kernel_check_y64: ALL GREEN — 9 shapes, EXACT arm bit-identical, RAND rms_rel <= 1.5e-6, codes 254/254 (log check-slice2-y64.log). Geometry does not touch exactness, same as v1.
verdict: NEGATIVE, both forms. Y=64 buys ONLY the tiny 5120->1024 shape (1.227x, the shape whose out_f=1024 gives just 16 row tiles at Y=64, so more CTAs is pure grid-fill) and is 0.7-1.7pp WORSE than slice 1 on every real shape. Y=128 with OCC=2 is 4-6pp worse everywhere: the 128x128 tile carries a 64-float accumulator per thread, so demanding 2 blocks/SM caps the register budget below what the mainloop needs and the kernel spills. MECHANISM NOTE: halving Y does not raise warps/SM at all — it splits the same 8 warps into two CTAs — so it buys grid parallelism, not latency hiding, and the v1 profile's 'latency-exposed at 1 CTA/SM' reading does not convert into throughput here.

change: cp.async double-buffer the weight tile against the MMA work (FP8_MMQ_PIPE=1, MEMRA_MMQ_PIPE_FP8 build knob): block 0 issued in a prologue, then every iteration issues block k+1's tile copy BEFORE computing block k, cp.async.wait_group 1 so the just-issued group stays in flight. Costs one extra x-tile buffer in smem (37KB -> 55KB total).
kernel_check: ALL GREEN — 9 shapes, EXACT arm bit-identical, RAND rms_rel <= 1.5e-6, codes 254/254 (log check-slice3-pipe.log)
verdict: NEGATIVE. 3-6pp WORSE than slice 1 on every shape. Mechanism: the ACTIVATION tile load is still a synchronous global->smem copy through the register file (18 KB per iteration at mmq_x=128, the same order as the 16 KB weight tile), and it sits between the cp.async issue and the wait. So the pipeline does not remove a stall — it adds a wait_group and 18 KB of smem pressure in front of a copy that was already being overlapped by the scheduler across the 8 resident warps. Overlapping the weight tile alone cannot pay while the y tile is synchronous and equally large.

hypothesis: v1's tile sweep found X=256 was its best geometry on the two largest shapes (down_proj 0.990, o_proj 0.956) but could not cross the floor — at MMQ_ITER_K=256 that tile needed 61+ KB of smem and ran 1 CTA/SM. Slice 1 halved the weight tile (37 KB at X=128), so X=256 should now be affordable. This is the ONE geometry re-test the halving licenses, not a fresh sweep.
change: FP8_MMQ_X=256 on the slice-1 kernel (PIPE=0, Y=128).
kernel_check: ALL GREEN — 9 shapes, EXACT bit-identical, RAND rms_rel <= 1.5e-6, codes 254/254 (log check-expA-x256.log)
verdict: POSITIVE, and the first time this kernel family has EXCEEDED the floor. m=6257: 4 of 6 shapes at or above 1.0x (o_proj 1.024, square 1.032, gate_up 1.007, q_proj 1.005). m=512: down_proj 1.084x, o_proj 1.001x, gate_up 0.997x, square 0.982x. The one consistent loser is 5120->1024 (0.522x at m=512): out_f=1024 gives only 8 row tiles at Y=128, and X=256 halves the token tiles to 2, so the whole grid is 16 CTAs on an 82-SM machine — a grid-shape fact about that projection, the same shape v1's X=64/Y=64 sweeps found anomalous in the opposite direction.

hypothesis: slice 3's own mechanism note said the cp.async weight pipeline could not pay because the SYNCHRONOUS activation tile sat between issue and wait and was the same size as the weight tile. X=256 doubles the MMA work per iteration against the same 16 KB weight copy, which is the condition under which overlap should start to pay. Testing the note rather than believing it.
verdict: NEGATIVE, and it CONFIRMS the slice-3 note. X=256 also doubles the y tile to 36 KB, so the synchronous activation copy grows exactly as fast as the MMA work it was supposed to hide behind; adding the second weight buffer on top (55 KB -> 91 KB of smem) then costs occupancy outright. Every shape is 5-10pp below the same geometry with PIPE=0. The weight tile is not the stall; cp.async on it is dead in both geometries, and the flag stays default 0. That is 2 of 2 bounded experiments spent.

final_default: FP8_MMQ_X=256 with a per-shape fallback to 128 when out_f < 2048 (FP8_MMQ_SMALL_OUT_F), Y=128, PIPE=0. The fallback exists because X=256 starves a narrow out_f: 5120->1024 measured 0.522x at X=256 vs 0.850x at X=128, and out_f is the only input the rule needs (m does not enter it). act_bytes overread pad raised from a hardcoded 128 to max(FP8_MMQ_X, FP8_MMQ_X_SMALL) so the widest selectable tile stays mapped.
kernel_check: ALL GREEN — 9 shapes, EXACT bit-identical, RAND rms_rel <= 1.5e-6, codes 254/254 (log check-final.log)
verdict: v2 BEATS the Q8_0 floor on 4 of 6 shapes at m=6257 (q_proj 1.046, gate_up 1.068, o_proj 1.024, square 1.021) and on down_proj at m=512 (1.087). Geometric mean vs floor: 1.014x at m=6257, 0.968x at m=512. v1 was 0.81-0.94x with NO shape at parity, so the recipe moved the kernel from uniformly-below-floor to at-or-above on the long-context shapes that dominate prefill. It does NOT clear ~1.1x on the aggregate, so the model-level battery threshold from the task is not met.

section: TOKEN-TILE SELECTION BUG — found by the local pp battery
what: the v2 default's fallback rule keyed on out_f alone (out_f < 2048 -> X=128), fit against the 27B's projection shapes. The local pp battery runs the qwen3-1.7B (hidden 2048, ffn 6144 -> out_f 1024..6144), where that rule picked X=256 for 4 of 5 projections and measured 0.535-0.865x floor against X=128's 0.847-0.890x on the same shapes in the same session. pp512 read 0.9808x floor as a direct consequence.
why_out_f_cannot_work: n_tokens sets the token-tile count, so the same out_f starves the grid at one m and fills it at another. An out_f threshold cannot express wave fill.
fix: compute both candidates' fill directly — ctas = row_tiles * token_tiles, fill = ctas / (waves * nsm) — and take the WIDE tile unless its fill drops below FP8_MMQ_FILL_MARGIN_PCT (86) percent of the narrow tile's. Wide preferred on ties (a wider token tile amortizes each weight-tile read over twice the MMA work). nsm cached per device ordinal: the rule runs on every prefill GEMM (25088 dispatches in one 1.7B 128-step stream), so a cudaDeviceGetAttribute per call would charge a driver round-trip to the kernel it selects for.
margin_fit: 86 is the measured separator. Tight pairs it splits: 27B q_proj m=512 fill-ratio 0.833 -> narrow (X=128 0.968 vs X=256 0.923); 27B gate_up m=512 0.875 -> wide (0.995 vs 0.973); 27B k/v_proj m=6257 exactly 0.850 -> narrow (X=128 0.951 vs X=256 0.913). The 1024-row shape stays narrow at every m tested, which is why 86 and not 85.
bench_change: fp8-mmq-bench gained a shape-set arg (27b|1p7b). A pp ratio measured on the 1.7B has to be explainable by THAT model's GEMM ratios — the 27B-only sheet is what let a rule calibrated on wide projections look correct.
kernel_check: ALL GREEN — 9 shapes, EXACT arm 0 bit mismatches + 0 NaN, RAND rms_rel <= 1.5e-6, codes 254/254 (log check-fill-rule.log). Selection is launch geometry; it does not touch the arithmetic.
logs: gemm-x128-1p7b-m512.log (the X=128 control that exposed it)
note: the 27B m=6257 sheet moved slightly vs the pre-fix run (o_proj 1.024->0.989, down 0.973->0.994, gate_up 1.068->0.993) because the fixed rule keeps k/v narrow and because these are separate sessions; both sheets are single-session interleaved medians and only the WITHIN-sheet ratios are comparable.

branch_applied: (b), same as v1: per-block-FP8 f32 accumulation is not Q8_0-requant s32 accumulation, so free-running stream identity is the wrong instrument and teacher forcing on the floor tape is the right one.
coverage: 25088 of 25216 prefill-GEMM hook entries dispatched = 99.5%. The 128 refusals are no_operand = the tied-embedding lm_head (one per step, 128 steps), which has no F8 source tensor. gate_off=0 bad_shape=0 bad_scale=0 nan=0. Floor control on the SAME binary: identical 25216 entries, all 25216 refused at the env gate, 0 dispatches — so a digest difference is the kernel, not run-to-run noise.

free_running_digests.floor: 0x85b3dfe4e7f01ec9 (bit-matches the v1 lane's recorded floor digest)

geometry_invariance: these digests and the 3/128 count reproduce EXACTLY across the pre-fix (out_f rule) and post-fix (wave-fill rule) binaries — the selection change moves which token tile runs, not the arithmetic, which is what the ARITHMETIC CONTRACT claims and this is the evidence for it.
flip_analysis: all 3 flips are near-ties: steps 23/29/67 at floor margins 0.023468 / 0.128180 / 0.171801 against a floor margin median of 3.6871 (mean 4.6930, sd 3.8392) — the 0.0th, 2.3th and 6.2th percentile, largest 0.047x the median, all within 1.22 sigma. Receipt: flip-margins.log.
six_draw: 2 disagreements in 192 sampled draws (d3 step 21 floor margin 0.237541 = 0.055x that draw's median; d5 step 0 floor margin 0.002348 = 0.0006x). 4 of 6 draws are 0/32. v1's count was 1/192 — same order, and both flips here are near-ties by the same measure.

quality_sanity_nll_at_1024.window: nll-window.txt, frozen held-out GSM8K test prose, no model-under-test output in it

vs_v1: v1 measured +0.11% perplexity on this same window and binary family; v2 is +0.0008%, i.e. ~130x closer to the floor — DESPITE v2's activation scale being 4x coarser (per-128 vs per-32). That is the e4m3-container argument holding up in practice: unlike int8, a coarser amax costs exponent headroom, not mantissa.

protocol: MEMRA_PP_ONLY=1 MEMRA_PP_REPS=3 in-process median; N=5 PROCESS reps per arm; arms INTERLEAVED (floor,mmq) inside each rep so clock/thermal drift hits both equally; flock /tmp/gpu5090.lock, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0; 1 Hz nvidia-smi sampler alongside. Floor re-measured in THIS session — v1's recorded floor is never used as a cross-day denominator. Two arms only: ARM A (MEMRA_FP8_FOLD) is not shippable and is not what v2 competes with.

pre_fix_same_battery.note: kept as the receipt for the selection bug: the pp512 gap is what sent the investigation to the 1.7B GEMM sheet.

reconciliation: the 1.7B's own GEMM sheet explains the pp numbers and bounds them. At m=512 every 1.7B projection measures 0.846-0.894x GEMM-only, yet pp512 is 0.9899x, because prefill is not all GEMM — attention, norms, rope and the lm_head are arm-independent, so a ~13% GEMM deficit dilutes to ~1%. At pp6257 the per-call m is capped by the engine's prefill chunk, so the 1.7B never reaches the m=6257 cells (1.000-1.064x) that would make this arm win end-to-end on this model.
verdict: NEGATIVE but nearly flat on the 1.7B: 0.9899x at pp512, 0.9951x at pp6257. This model's projections are too narrow for the arm's advantage to appear; the shapes where v2 beats the floor (27B m=6257, 1.7B m=6257) are not the shapes this checkpoint presents at the engine's chunk size.
